listed.verification: This model is on Govee's list of LAN Control models. The toolkit sends it the commands that Govee documents for that list, and that the model's own controls admit. Nobody has tested them on this one yet. Report what you observe, and the model gets a device file of its own.

home.title: Control your Govee lights from your own machine.
home.lede: Your lights stay on your network, and your commands stay there with them: over Wi-Fi, over Bluetooth, from a lighting desk in DMX, or through the cloud on the days you are away.
home.strip_title: Paint the zones, not the whole light.
home.strip_lede: A light strip draws one zone per address on the wire.
home.strip_hint: The strip below lights the zones a pointer passes over.
home.zone_text: Address a single zone, a range or the whole strip, inside the same frame.
home.effects_text: A wave, a gradient, a progress bar across the zones: you write the animation, and the strip draws it.
home.frames_text: Hold the channel open and keep sending. Music, screen, a sensor: the strip follows.
home.features_lede: Drive your lights, paint them zone by zone, play a scene. Each one is a single line in a terminal or in your code.
home.basics_text: The everyday commands, from a script, a shortcut or your home automation.
home.segments_text: Give each zone of your strip its own color.
home.realtime_text: Send frame after frame. The light follows your music, your screen or any source.
home.scenes_text: Hundreds of ready-made scenes, one command away.
home.music_text: Your light listens through its own microphone and follows the beat.
home.draw_text: Paint your light zone by zone and give it a motion of your own.
home.engine_lede: From code, a terminal, a lighting desk or an assistant: one engine does the work under each of them.
home.rust_text: The engine itself. Every other language takes its behavior from here.
home.cli_text: Type one line in a terminal and the light answers right away.
home.python_text: A few lines of Python and your lights follow. Install it with pip.
home.node_text: Drive the lights from JavaScript or TypeScript. Install it with npm.
home.mcp_text: Ask your assistant to set a light. The MCP server hands it the controls.
home.lan_text: Everything, segments included. Turn on "LAN Control" in the Govee app first.
home.ble_text: Works over Bluetooth alone. It also puts a new device on your network.
home.cloud_text: Through Govee's own API, with a key. The everyday commands, from anywhere.

home3.sdk_title: A few lines, and the light answers.
home3.title: Your Govee lights. Instant. Local. Yours.
home3.lede: Control every light at home from one free app. Commands go straight to your lights over Wi-Fi, so they react the moment you click.
home3.meta: Free and open source · Works on your home Wi-Fi
home3.benefits_lede: Everything you expect from your lights, and a few things you didn't.
home3.instant_text: No round trip through a server. Your light reacts as fast as your Wi-Fi.
home3.zones_text: Give each zone its own color, or stream colors live from your screen or your code.
home3.scenes_text: Hundreds of ready-made scenes. Or let your light follow the beat.
home3.studio_text: One app for all your lights. Rooms, colors, zones and scenes.
home3.dmx_text: Run your lights from a lighting desk, like any stage fixture.
home3.sdk_text: Rust, Python, Node.js, a CLI and an MCP server for AI assistants. One core, same behavior everywhere.
home3.studio_lede: Studio spots every light on your network. Give them names, put them in rooms, and set the mood in a click.
home3.studio_tick_zones: Customize each zone of a light strip
home3.studio_tick_phone: Use it from your phone or tablet too
home3.dmx_lede: Your lighting desk sees each light as a regular fixture. Patch it, program it, run the show.
home3.dmx_tick_resolution: One color per light, per zone or per LED
home3.sdk_lede: The protocol lives once, in Rust. Python and Node.js bind to that core, so every language behaves the same. Stream frames in real time, or hand the controls to your AI assistant over MCP.
home3.modes_lede: You choose how each light is reached.
home3.lan_text: At home, on the same network. Every feature, zone by zone. Switch on "LAN Control" in the Govee Home app first.
home3.ble_text: No Wi-Fi needed. Also helps you add a new light to your network.
home3.cloud_text: The everyday controls when you're away, with an API key.
home3.closer_lede: Type your model and find out what it can do.
home3.closer_meta: Free and open source, MIT license
pdev.title: Build with your lights.
pdev.lede: One Rust core, bound to Python and Node.js. Every language behaves the same, from a one-line script to a real-time stream.
pdev.closer_lede: Read the code, open an issue, add your light.
pstudio.title: Every light, one app.
pstudio.lede: Studio finds the lights on your network, puts them in rooms and sets them from your own computer. Open it on a phone or a tablet of the same network, too.
pstudio.find_text: One scan lists every light on the network. Name each one as you add it.
pstudio.rooms_text: Drag a light onto a room. A light can sit in several rooms at once.
pstudio.color_text: A color wheel, white and brightness for each light. Keep your favorite colors at hand.
pstudio.segments_text: Select segments of a strip and paint them, or lay a gradient across it.
pstudio.phone_text: Share Studio on your network and open it from a phone or a tablet.
pstudio.backup_text: Export the whole configuration to one file, and restore it when you need it.
pstudio.library_text: Your presets and scenes in one place. A preset is a look. A scene plays looks on a timeline.
pstudio.live_text: Play your presets and scenes from a grid of pads, with a tap or a key.
pstudio.stage_text: Place the lights of a room in 3D, then compose scenes on a timeline, in time with the music.
pstudio.get_lede: The Studio server carries the whole interface. Install it, start it, and open the address in a browser.
pstudio.linux: On Linux, a systemd service starts Studio at boot.
pstudio.local: Studio listens on this computer alone until you share it with your network from its settings.
pdmx.title: Your lights, patched on the desk.
pdmx.lede: govee-dmx takes the Art-Net your desk already sends and writes it to each light over {{badge_lan}}. Your lights become fixtures of the show.
pdmx.layouts_lede: A desk calls a layout a personality. Channels 1 to 3 are the same on every model, so a cue carries from one light to the next.
pdmx.full: 6 channels. One color for the whole light.
pdmx.segment: 3 channels, plus 3 per segment. One color per segment.
pdmx.pixel: 3 channels, plus 3 per LED. One color per LED.
pdmx.layouts_note: Each model serves the layouts its hardware carries. Its page on the device list prints the channel table.
pdmx.steps_title: From nothing to a node in three commands
pdmx.patch_text: govee-dmx patch finds the lights and gives each one a free start address. It keeps every address you set.
pdmx.identify_text: govee-dmx identify lights one fixture at a time and names its line in the patch file.
pdmx.run_text: govee-dmx run answers the desk poll and drives the lights. The rig comes up dark.
pdmx.dry_text: --dry-run prints what each fixture reads and leaves the lights as they are.
pdmx.drop: When a light drops off the network, the others carry on and the run reports it.
pdmx.need: You need a light that {{badge_lan}} reaches, and a desk, a media server or a show program that sends Art-Net.
psdk.title: One engine, in your language.
psdk.lede: The protocol lives once, in Rust. Python and Node.js bind to that core, and the command line reads the same device files. Each one behaves the same way.
psdk.rust: The engine itself, async on Tokio. Every other language takes its behavior from here.
psdk.cli: Type one line in a terminal and the light answers right away.
psdk.python: An asyncio API. The wheel carries the device catalog, so pip install is the whole install.
psdk.node: JavaScript or TypeScript, with types. npm install is the whole install.
psdk.modes_text: You enable each mode per device.
psdk.basics_text: On, off, color, brightness, from a script or your home automation.
psdk.segments_text: Give each segment of a strip its own color.
psdk.scenes_text: Play a ready-made scene, or store a drawing of your own on the light.
pstudio.description: Find your lights, put them in rooms and set them in one app, on your own computer.
pdmx.description: Patch your lights on a lighting desk. The bridge turns Art-Net into frames on the local network.
psdk.description: Drive your lights from Rust, Python, Node.js or a terminal. One engine under each of them.

devices.more_title: Your light does more than this?
devices.more_text: The list shows what each model answers today. Follow the guide and add what your light does, or a model that is missing, or mail us the light and we add it.
add.title: Your light does more. Let's add it.
add.lede:
A capability or a model joins this list when somebody tests it:
you, or us after one email.
add.one_tag: Lane one · your hands, your light
add.one_text: The light stays on your shelf and you drive the whole thing. The guide walks you through it end to end: what to fill in, what to record, and how to check your work before you send it.
add.one_1: Open the guide and copy the example file.
add.one_2: Fill in what your light answers.
add.one_3: Send it in. We read it with you.
add.one_4: Your name sits on the model page.
add.one_note: Some terminal time. Ask us anything on the way.
add.two_tag: Lane two · we do the work
add.two_title: Mail us, then mail us the light.
add.two_text: Write to us and we send you back our address. You buy the light, you have it shipped straight to that address, and then you forget about it. We plug it in, we listen to what it says, and we write its file.
add.two_1: You send one email with the model code of each light you want.
add.two_2: We answer with the address the parcel goes to.
add.two_3: The light lands on our desk.
add.two_4: Within a week, what your light does is on this site.
add.two_note: The light stays on our shelf.
add.small_title: The small print, which is small
add.a1: Any one that does more than its page shows, or that is missing from this list. A strip, a bulb, a lamp, a panel: if it lights up and it is a Govee, it is welcome. A model with the i mark on the device list is the easy kind, and it still needs somebody to confirm it.
add.q2: Where does my light end up?
add.a2: On our shelf, for good. It is your contribution to the project, and it earns its keep there: it answers questions long after its page goes up, every time the firmware changes. Take lane one if you would rather keep yours.
add.a3: Then the page says so, in those words: untested, which is a long way from broken.
add.q4: I want to help, and my lights are staying put.
add.a4: Take a look at the source. Reports, notes and corrections all land in the same place.
